content_custody.retrieval_reproducibility: The owner page is mutable and supplies no immutable byte archive. The URI may later return different bytes; exact reproduction requires retained bytes matching this digest.

claims_used.claim: The guidance identifies isolated independent subtasks as one use of parallel calls and programmatic aggregation.
claims_used.evidence_excerpt: Breaking a task into independent subtasks run in parallel.

transfer_limits: This is practitioner guidance, not a controlled comparison of SLEC-1.
It does not establish assessor independence, routing accuracy, or effectiveness for this repository.
The mapping from generic parallel sectioning to exactly four slot-local assessors is a proposal constraint, not a result reported by the source.
contradictions_or_tensions: Parallel calls trade additional latency and cost for easier subtasks; four assessors therefore require bounded evaluation rather than an assumed benefit.

identity.title: Zero Trust Architecture
identity.owner: National Institute of Standards and Technology

content_custody.retrieval_reproducibility: The DOI and NIST URL identify the publication but do not cryptographically promise the same future bytes. Exact reproduction requires retained PDF bytes matching this digest.

claims_used.claim: The zero-trust tenets reject automatic trust based on network location.
claims_used.evidence_excerpt: Network location alone does not imply trust.

claims_used.claim: The zero-trust tenets call for per-session decisions for individual resources and deny automatic authority propagation to another resource.
claims_used.evidence_excerpt: Access to individual enterprise resources is granted on a per-session basis.

transfer_limits: The publication concerns enterprise zero-trust architecture, not model routing.
Its tenets motivate explicit trust boundaries but do not validate the local broker or prove that a capability digest is sufficient authorization.
Per-session enterprise access is translated only as a conservative per-request broker rule.
Fail-closed and complete-local-mediation rules are conservative design inferences from rejecting implicit trust and evaluating each resource request; NIST does not specify this broker.
contradictions_or_tensions: A full zero-trust deployment is broader than a small local reference broker; importing the whole architecture would violate the simplicity constraint.

content_custody.retrieval_reproducibility: The date-versioned documentation URL is a mutable publisher endpoint, not a content-addressed archive. Exact reproduction requires retained bytes matching this digest.

claims_used.claim: The guidance recommends minimal default privileges and restricted filesystem, network, and system-resource access for locally launched MCP servers.
claims_used.evidence_excerpt: sandboxed environment with minimal default privileges

claims_used.claim: The guidance identifies time-of-check to time-of-use risk and recommends binding a validated resolution result through use.

pinpoint.section: Server-Side Request Forgery, Mitigation, DNS Resolution Considerations

claims_used.evidence_excerpt: pinning DNS resolution results between check and use

claims_used.claim: By least-privilege analogy, progressive scope minimization motivates withholding task and capsule data from the reference broker.
claims_used.evidence_excerpt: Implement a progressive, least-privilege scope model

transfer_limits: The guidance covers MCP implementations broadly; SLEC-1 is not itself an MCP authorization implementation.
The source supports threat selection and conservative local controls, not a security certification.
DNS pinning is analogous to, but does not itself specify, regular-file descriptor custody; task-data withholding and the fixed least-reference rule are explicit least-privilege inferences.
contradictions_or_tensions: The guide recommends environment-dependent defenses; a portable local broker can enforce file custody but cannot claim host-wide sandboxing.

identity.title: JSON Schema: A Media Type for Describing JSON Documents
identity.owner: Internet Engineering Task Force archive; JSON Schema project
identity.version: Draft 2020-12, draft-bhutton-json-schema-01; archived draft text dated 2022-06-10; canonical HTML reports 2022-06-16

content_custody.digest_scope: complete version-numbered IETF Internet-Draft archive text response body
content_custody.retrieval_reproducibility: The numbered IETF Internet-Draft archive is version-pinned. Exact reproduction is verified by the declared digest over the complete archived text bytes.

claims_used.claim: JSON Schema assertions can express pass-or-fail constraints on JSON documents; closedness remains a property of the selected schema, not an automatic guarantee.
claims_used.evidence_excerpt: assert constraints on a JSON document

claims_used.claim: The prefixItems applicator validates array elements against schemas at corresponding positions, supporting an ordered tuple contract.
claims_used.evidence_excerpt: each element of the instance validates against the schema at the same position

claims_used.claim: Because only declared assertions can fail an instance, separate deterministic checks are required for semantic anchors, byte custody, and filesystem invariants outside the schema.

transfer_limits: Schema conformance establishes declared structural constraints only; it does not establish semantic-anchor validity, byte custody, order outside declared arrays, or filesystem safety.
The archived core document relies on companion vocabularies for many validation keywords; SLEC-1 must declare and enforce its chosen dialect and keywords.
A schema can remain valid while being too permissive, so unexpected fields and non-schema invariants require explicit deterministic checks.
contradictions_or_tensions: The specification permits extensibility and annotations, while this proposal deliberately selects closed structures and treats undeclared fields as invalid.

claims_used.claim: The procedure selects its control parameter from observed calibration data.

pinpoint.section: 1.1 Algorithm and Preview of Main Results

claims_used.claim: The paper states that its conformal-risk-control algorithm does not control risk without the monotonicity assumption.

transfer_limits: SLEC-1 has no independently justified calibration population, monotone loss family, exchangeability argument, or sample size for a conformal guarantee.
A conformal threshold would introduce observed-data-dependent selection into a mechanism required to be fixed before held-out evaluation.
Rejecting this method does not show that fixed deterministic rules are statistically optimal; it only prevents an unsupported guarantee and an incompatible calibration path.
contradictions_or_tensions: The method can offer stronger statistical guarantees when its prerequisites hold, but those prerequisites are absent here; using it would overstate evidence and add unjustified machinery.

cross_source_constraints.rule: Use four independently produced slot-local capsules and a deterministic parent fold; no assessor receives another slot or another assessor output.
Any invalid, missing, duplicate, uncertain, digest-mismatched, or anchor-invalid capsule produces no selection.
Broker at most two fixed capability IDs into at most one digest-pinned local regular file per slot, without task or capsule data.
A path, type, size, digest, or time-of-check failure discards the entire request without partial bytes.
Use fixed deterministic abstention rules and retain a structural-proposal-only claim ceiling.

forbidden_bindings: calibration thresholds derived from evaluation data
conclusion: The five-source packet supports a bounded, independently assessed, deterministic, least-privilege proposal and its falsifiers. The unavailable Saltzer preprint custody was removed rather than treated as evidence; simplicity, fail-closed mediation, and least-reference constraints therefore rest on conservative cross-source inferences from Anthropic, NIST, and MCP guidance. The packet does not establish activation quality, runtime behavior, provider behavior, security certification, product value, or promotion readiness.
